title: Build a complex diagram up step by step
statement: Build a complex diagram one element at a time as each is named, rather than opening on the finished, fully labelled picture.
example: Across 56 studies, segmenting improved retention by d = 0.32 and transfer by d = 0.36.
detail: The grade-7 science visual design guide builds complex diagrams progressively, one spoken idea at a time, because a complete diagram presents many relations before the learner has names for them; its example starts with the cell boundary, adds the nucleus and then the mitochondria as each is named, and reassembles the labelled cell only for the recap (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-visuals-human-v0.1.md`, lines 100-113). It cites segmenting at d=0.32 for retention, d=0.36 for transfer and d=0.23 for cognitive load across 56 studies (Rey et al. 2019). For low-prior-knowledge learners it adds that watching a diagram being drawn beat receiving it pre-drawn, d=0.58 with a visible body and d=0.35 with a visible hand (Fiorella & Mayer 2016).
against: Drawing helped only with a visible body or hand: hand-less animated drawing was d=-0.16 in the same guide (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-visuals-human-v0.1.md`, lines 105-109), and another record reads the drawing study's transfer benefits as conditional rather than universal. The guide's budget of about four new elements per scene is an operating heuristic, not a tested limit (lines 245-246).

evidence.quote: **Evidence.** Segmenting improves retention (*d*=0.32), transfer (*d*=0.36), and cognitive load (*d*=0.23) across 56 studies [11]. For low-prior-knowledge learners, watching a diagram be drawn beats receiving it pre-drawn: *d*=0.58 with a visible body and *d*=0.35 with a visible hand; hand-less animated drawing was *d*=-0.16 [16].

Start with the cell boundary, add the nucleus when named, then add mitochondria when named. After the naming pass, reassemble the labeled cell for the recap. Do not begin with twelve labeled organelles.
A per-scene budget of about four new elements is an [OH], not an experimentally fixed limit
